evidence: packages/core/videoClient.ts:26 awaits appStore[appName], which is a bundled local import() promise. It can only reject if a module fails to load. Before this PR the same failure was a static import error that stopped the whole module graph from loading, so the PR adds no new per-provider failure mode. The comment is also wrong about createMeeting: its `await getVideoAdapters([credential])` at line 52 sits outside the try block that starts at line 69, so createMeeting has no fallback for this either. updateMeeting (line 111), deleteMeeting (line 144) and getBusyVideoTimes (line 38, called from packages/core/getBusyTimes.ts:137) do await without a catch, and a rejection in getBusyVideoTimes would fail the whole busy-times call. Wrapping the lookup per credential would help a little, but the scenario is a broken build.

The for loop at packages/core/videoClient.ts:24-33 does not load anything in sequence. Every import() in packages/app-store/index.ts:3-30 starts when that module is first evaluated, so the loop only awaits promises that are already running or already settled; after the first load each await is just a microtask. Also, all call sites except getBusyVideoTimes pass one credential (lines 52, 111, 144, 162, 185, 206). Promise.all would give no real gain.

packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125 uses forEach(async ...), so the promises are not awaited, and the try/catch at lines 124-139 cannot catch errors from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. They surface as unhandled rejections, which is worse than 'silently swallowed'. Most of this predates the PR: the base code's sync callback also returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises that forEach threw away. What the PR adds is that getCalendar is now awaited inside the callback, so a failure there also escapes the catch. Using await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try would fix both.

packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 is the same as vital/lib/reschedule.ts (diff shows only a comment differs). forEach(async ...) is fire-and-forget, so sendRequestRescheduleEmail (~line 143) and `return true` can run before the deletions finish. That ordering was already the case before the PR, because the base forEach also dropped the returned deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises. The PR only moves getCalendar into the async callback. Worth fixing with Promise.all, but the problem is mostly pre-existing.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553-567: forEach(async ...) returns promises nobody awaits, and sendRequestRescheduleEmail at line 570 does not wait for the deletions. There is no try/catch here, so a rejection is unhandled. The base code already dropped the deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises the same way, so the ordering and error-propagation gap predates the PR; the PR only adds the awaited getCalendar inside the callback. Promise.all over a map would fix it.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:589-596: the paymentApp lookup and `new PaymentService(paymentAppCredential)` are outside the try at lines 597-605 that calls handleRefundError. That structure already existed in the base commit; the PR only adds `await`, which can reject only if the bundled stripepayment module fails to load. The not-implemented case returns null (line 592) instead of throwing, and nearby failures such as 'Payment app credentials not found' (line 583) also throw outside the refund handler by design. The claim is technically accurate but describes a pre-existing, unlikely path.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:458-470: `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)` plus `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` (line 467) pushes an already-resolved value after an await. The recurring-event deletions are therefore never tracked by `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, and their errors are unhandled. The base commit had the same forEach(async) and the same push-after-await. The PR's `await getCalendar` (line 461) only delays when the deletes start; it does not change tracking. The claim that the handler reaches Promise.all before the deletes start is unlikely, because several prisma awaits come before line 652. Real bug, but pre-existing.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:28-29: getCalendarCredentials stores getCalendar(credential), now a Promise, in the `calendar` field. The only reader, getConnectedCalendars, awaits it (line 48). Other callers (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer.tsx:340,415; apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts:83) only pass the result to getConnectedCalendars. TypeScript infers Promise<Calendar | null>, so a consumer that forgot to await would get a type error. Renaming is optional.

packages/app-store/index.ts:3-30: the object literal calls import("./x") for all 28 apps when the module is evaluated, so the first import of appStore (e.g. packages/core/videoClient.ts:4, packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts) starts loading every provider at once. This defeats on-demand loading, which is the stated goal of the PR. It also means a failed load in any provider that is never awaited becomes an unhandled rejection. Lazy thunks (`zoomvideo: () => import("./zoomvideo")`) with call sites changed to `await appStore[name]?.()` would load providers on demand.
